For  $D$  and  $f$  as in the lemma statement and  $y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)$ , let  $u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}\in H_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}\cap\overline{D}$  be chosen in an arbitrary manner (as in Lemma A.4 with  $n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon$  in place of  $\varepsilon$ ).
By Lemma A.4 applied with  $n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon$  in place of  $\varepsilon$ , if  $\beta>0$  is chosen to be sufficiently small (depending only on  $\gamma$ ) then there exists  $\alpha_{0}=\alpha_{0}(\gamma)>0$  such that with polynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$ , it holds simultaneously for every choice of  $D$  and  $f$  as in the lemma statement that
$\displaystyle(n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)^{-1}\int_{D}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+(n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)^{-1+\alpha_{0}}$
$\displaystyle\leq\sum_{y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)}f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})$
$\displaystyle\qquad\leq(n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)^{-1}\int_{B_{(n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)^{\alpha_{0}}}(D)}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+(n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)^{-1+\alpha_{0}}.$
(A.35)
Fix  $q\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(0,\tfrac{2}{(2+\gamma)^{2}}}}\right)$  chosen in a manner depending only on  $\gamma$ .
By Lemma 2.4 (applied with  $\varepsilon^{1/2}$  in place of  $\varepsilon$ ) and our choice of  $n_{\varepsilon}$ , it holds with polynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$  that
$\operatorname{diam}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(H_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}}}\right)\leq\varepsilon^{q/2},\quad\forall y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(B_{\rho}).$
(A.36)
By Lemma A.8 (applied with  $m=\lfloor(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{2}\varepsilon^{-1/4}\rfloor$ , say) and a union bound, it holds with superpolynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$  that, in the notation of that lemma,
$\operatorname{Perim}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}}\right)\leq(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{2}\varepsilon^{-1/4},\quad\forall y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(B_{\rho}).$
(A.37)
By [GMS19, Lemma 2.6], it holds with superpolynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$  that
$\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)\leq(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{2},\quad\forall x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(B_{\rho}).$
(A.38)
Fix  $\zeta\in(0,1)$  to be chosen later, in a manner depending only on  $q,\gamma$ .
By Lemma 2.4 (applied with  $n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon$  in place of  $\varepsilon$ ), the fact that the cells of  $\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}$  have LQG mass  $n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon\approx\varepsilon^{1/2}$ , and a standard estimate for the  $\gamma$ -LQG area measure (e.g., [GHS19a, Lemma A.3] together with the Chebyshev inequality) it holds with polynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$  that
$\#\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(B_{\rho+\varepsilon^{q/2}})\leq\varepsilon^{-1/2-\zeta}$
(A.39)
Henceforth assume that (A.35) through (A.39) hold, which happens with polynomially high probability as  $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$ .
We will check that (A.15) holds simultaneously for every choice of  $D,f$  as in the lemma statement provided  $\zeta$  and  $\beta$  are chosen to be sufficiently small (depending only on  $q,\gamma$ ).
Step 2: summing the degrees of vertices of  $\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$ .
For a vertex  $x\in\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}\setminus\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$ , the degree  $\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})$  of  $x$  as a vertex of  $\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$  is the same as  $\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)$ . If  $x\in\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$  we still have  $\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})\leq\deg^{\varepsilon}(x)$  but the inequality might be strict since  $x$  can have edges to vertices in  $\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}\setminus(y-n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon,y]$ .
Therefore,
$\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)$
$\displaystyle=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}\setminus\mathcal{V}(\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}(\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)$
$\displaystyle\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}),\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})+\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}(\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)}}\right].$
(A.40)
The sum of the degrees  $\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})$  over all  $x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$  is precisely twice the number of edges of  $\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$ . Recall that  $\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$  has  $n_{\varepsilon}$  vertices and is a triangulation with boundary.
By Lemma A.7 followed by (A.37),
$\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}(x;\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})=6n_{\varepsilon}+6-2\operatorname{Perim}(\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[6n_{\varepsilon}-2(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{2}\varepsilon^{-1/4},6n_{\varepsilon}}}\right].$
(A.41)
By (A.37) and (A.38), we also have
$\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}(\partial\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon})}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)\leq(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{4}\varepsilon^{-1/4}.$
(A.42)
By plugging (A.41) and (A.42) into (A.40), we get
$\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[6n_{\varepsilon}-2(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{2}\varepsilon^{-1/4},6n_{\varepsilon}+(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{4}\varepsilon^{-1/4}}}\right].$
(A.43)
Step 3: summing  $f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})$  over vertices of  $\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$ .
If  $x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$ , then both  $w_{x}^{\varepsilon}$  and  $u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}$  lie in  $H_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}$  so by (A.36) and the  $\varepsilon^{-\beta}$ -Lipschitz continuity of  $f$ ,
$|f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})-f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})|\leq\varepsilon^{q/2-\beta}.$
(A.44)
By (A.44), then (A.43) and the fact that  $\#\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}=n_{\varepsilon}\approx\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ ,
$\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)$
$\displaystyle\qquad\in\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})-\varepsilon^{q/2-\beta}}}\right)\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x),\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})+\varepsilon^{q/2-\beta}}}\right)\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}}\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)}}\right]$
$\displaystyle\qquad\subset\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[6n_{\varepsilon}f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})-2\varepsilon^{q/2-1/2-\beta},6n_{\varepsilon}f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})+2\varepsilon^{q/2-1/2-\beta}}}\right],$
(A.45)
where in the last line we used that  $\|f\|_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon^{-\beta}$  and we absorbed the polylogarithmic factors from the error terms in (A.43) into powers of  $\varepsilon$  (which we can do since  $q<1/2$ ).
Step 4: conclusion.
Each  $x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(D)$  is contained in  $\mathcal{V}\mathcal{T}_{y}^{\varepsilon}$  for a unique choice of  $y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)$ .
By summing the upper bound in (A.45) over all  $y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)$ , we get
$\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(D)}f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)\leq 6n_{\varepsilon}\sum_{y\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(D)}f(u_{y}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon})+2\varepsilon^{q/2-1/2-\beta}\#\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D).$
(A.46)
From (A.39) we get  $\#\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)\leq\varepsilon^{-1/2-\zeta}$ .
By applying this and the upper bound in (A.35) to estimate the right side of (A.46), we obtain
$\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(D)}f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x)$
$\displaystyle\leq 6\varepsilon^{-1}\int_{D}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+n_{\varepsilon}^{\alpha_{0}}\varepsilon^{-1+\alpha_{0}}+O_{\varepsilon}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\varepsilon^{q/2-1-\beta-\zeta}}}\right)$
$\displaystyle\leq 6\varepsilon^{-1}\int_{D}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+O_{\varepsilon}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\varepsilon^{-1+\alpha}}}\right)$
for any choice of  $\alpha<\min\{\alpha_{0},\,q/2-\beta-\zeta\}$ .
If we choose  $\zeta$  and  $\beta$  sufficiently small, in a manner depending only on  $q,\gamma$ , then we can arrange that this minimum is positive.
Thus, after possibly slightly shrinking  $\alpha$  we get that the upper bound in (A.21) holds for small enough  $\varepsilon>0$ .
We similarly obtain the lower bound in (A.21) using the lower bounds in each of (A.35) and (A.43).
∎
A.3 Space-filling SLE loops
Let  $\kappa>4$ , let  $D\subset\mathbbm{C}$  be a simply connected domain, and let  $a\in\partial D$  be a prime end. The purpose of this section is to explain one possible definition of the counterclockwise space-filling SLE loop  $\eta$  in  $D$  based at  $a$ , and to show that this space-filling SLE loop can be obtained as the limit (for a rather strong notion of convergence) of space-filling SLE from  $a$  to  $b$  in  $D$  as  $b\rightarrow a$  from the clockwise direction.
The proofs in this section are based on the theory of imaginary geometry from [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17].
We will mostly focus on the case when  $(D,a)=(\mathbbm{H},\infty)$ ; the space-filling SLE loop for other choices of  $(D,a)$  will be defined via conformal mapping.
Fix  $\kappa>4$ . As in [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17], we define the constant
$\lambda^{\prime}:=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\kappa}}.$
(A.47)
Note that our  $\kappa$  is called  $\kappa^{\prime}$  in [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17].
Let  $h$  be a zero-boundary GFF on  $\mathbbm{H}$  plus the constant  $-\lambda^{\prime}$ . For  $z\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$ , let  $\eta^{z,L}$  (resp.  $\eta^{z,R}$ ) be the flow line of  $h$  started from  $z$  with angle  $\pi/2$  (resp.  $-\pi/2$ ) and stopped at the first time it hits  $\mathbbm{R}$ , as defined in [MS17, Theorem 1.1]. The law of  $\eta^{z,L}$  is locally absolutely continuous w.r.t. that of a SLE ${}_{16/\kappa}(16/\kappa-2)$  curve in any interval of time before it hits  $\mathbbm{R}$ . By [MS17, Theorem 1.9], for distinct  $z,w\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$ , a.s. the curves  $\eta^{z,L}$  and  $\eta^{w,L}$  (resp.  $\eta^{z,L}$  and  $\eta^{w,R}$ ) a.s. merge into each other after some finite time.
We define a total order  $\preceq$  on  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  by declaring that  $z\preceq w$  if and only if  $z$  lies in a connected component of  $\mathbbm{H}\setminus(\eta^{w,L}\cup\eta^{w,R})$  whose boundary is traced by the left side of  $\eta^{w,L}$  and the right side of  $\eta^{w,R}$ .
For  $a<0$ , let  $\eta_{a}$  be a chordal space-filling SLEκ from  $a$  to  $\infty$ .
Let  $\preceq_{a}$  be the total order on  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  induced by  $\eta_{a}$ , i.e.,  $z\preceq_{a}w$  if and only if  $\eta_{a}$  hits  $z$  before  $w$ .
Due to the construction of space-filling SLEκ in [MS17, Section 1.2.3], the ordering  $\preceq_{a}$  admits the following equivalent description.
Let  $h_{a}$  be a GFF on  $\mathbbm{H}$  with boundary data  $\lambda^{\prime}$  on  $(-\infty,a]$  and  $-\lambda^{\prime}$  on  $[a,\infty)$ .
Then we can realize  $\eta_{a}$  as the space-filling SLEκ counterflow line of  $h_{a}$  from  $a$  to  $\infty$ .
Furthermore, if we define the flow lines  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  and  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$  for  $z\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  in the same manner as  $\eta^{z,L}$  and  $\eta^{z,R}$  above but with  $h_{a}$  in place of  $h$ , then for  $z\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  the curves  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  and  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$  are the left and right outer boundaries of  $\eta_{a}$  stopped at the first time it hits  $z$ . We note that  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  (resp.  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$ ) stops upon hitting  $(-\infty,a]$  (resp.  $[a,\infty)$ ).
Consequently, the ordering  $\preceq_{a}$  can be defined in the same manner as the ordering  $\preceq$  above but with  $h_{a}$  in place of  $h$ .
Proposition A.10.
There is a unique continuous curve  $\eta:\mathbbm{R}\rightarrow\overline{\mathbbm{H}}$  from  $\infty$  to  $\infty$  which satisfies  $\eta(0)=0$  and  $\operatorname{area}\eta([s,t])=t-s$  for each  $s<t$ , hits the points of  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  in the order specified by  $\preceq$ , and fills in all of  $\mathbbm{H}$ .
The law of  $\eta$  is scale and translation invariant in the sense that for  $C>0$  and  $b\in\mathbbm{R}$ , we have  $C\eta+b\overset{d}{=}\eta$  viewed as curves modulo time parametrization.
Moreover, for each fixed  $r>0$  it holds that  $\preceq_{a}|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  converges to  $\preceq|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  in the total variation sense as  $a\rightarrow-\infty$ .
Definition A.11.
The curve  $\eta$  of Proposition A.10 is defined to be the counterclockwise space-filling SLEκ loop based at  $\infty$  in  $\mathbbm{H}$ .
The clockwise space-filling SLEκ loop based at  $\infty$  in  $\mathbbm{H}$  is the curve  $\widetilde{\eta}$  which is the image of  $\eta$  under the anticonformal map  $x+iy\mapsto-x+iy$ .
For a domain  $D$  and a prime end  $b\in\partial D$ , we define the counterclockwise (resp. clockwise) space-filling SLEκ loop based at  $b$  in  $D$  to be the image of  $\eta$  (resp.  $\widetilde{\eta}$ ) under a conformal map  $\mathbbm{H}\rightarrow D$  which takes  $\infty$  to  $b$ , viewed as a curve modulo time parametrization (the law of this curve does not depend on the choice of conformal map due to the scale / translation invariance property of  $\eta$ ).
It is possible to establish the existence of the curve  $\eta$  of Proposition A.10 by repeating essentially the same arguments used in [MS17] to construct space-filling SLE with distinct starting and ending points. However, in order to make our proof easier to follow and to get the total variation convergence statement, we will instead deduce Proposition A.10 from existing results in the literature. The key idea of the proof is that when  $a$  is very negative, the restrictions of  $h$  and  $h_{a}$  to a fixed neighborhood of 0 in  $\mathbbm{H}$  are close in the total variation sense, and moreover the orderings  $\preceq$  and  $\preceq_{a}$  are in a certain sense locally determined by  $h$  and  $h_{a}$ , respectively.
Let us now specify a precise version of the locality property of  $\preceq_{a}$ .
For a radius  $\rho>0$ , let  $T_{a}^{\rho}$  (resp.  $S_{a}^{\rho}$ ) be the first time that  $\eta_{a}$  enters  $B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}$  before hitting  $0$  (resp. the last time that  $\eta_{a}$  enters  $B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}$  after hitting 0).
We define
$\eta_{a}^{\rho}:=\eta_{a}|_{[T_{a}^{\rho},S_{a}^{\rho}]}\quad\text{and}\quad K_{a}^{\rho}:=\eta_{a}([T_{a}^{\rho},S_{a}^{\rho}]).$
(A.48)
We now describe  $K_{a}^{\rho}$  in terms of  $\preceq_{a}$ .
Lemma A.12.
Let  $\eta_{a}^{0,L}$  be the flow line of  $h_{a}$  started from 0 with angle  $\pi/2$ .
If  $z\in B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$ , then  $z\in K_{a}^{\rho}$  if and only if  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  merges into  $\eta_{a}^{0,L}$  before leaving  $B_{\rho}(0)$  and  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$  hits  $[a,\infty)$  before leaving  $B_{\rho}(0)$ .
Proof.
This follows since  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  and  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$  are the left/right outer boundaries of  $\eta_{a}$  at the (a.s. unique) time when it hits  $a$  and  $\eta_{a}^{0,L}$  is the outer boundary of  $\eta_{a}$  at the (a.s. unique) time when it hits 0.
∎
As a consequence of Lemma A.12 and the fact that the flow lines  $\eta_{a}^{z,L}$  and  $\eta_{a}^{z,R}$  are locally determined by  $h$  (c.f. the proof of [GMS19, Lemma 2.4]), it follows that  $\preceq_{a}|_{K_{a}^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}}$  is a.s. determined by  $h_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$ .
Let  $\eta^{0,L}$  be the flow line of  $h$  started from 0 with angle  $\pi/2$ .
Let  $K^{\rho}$  be the closure of the set of  $z\in B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}$  such that  $z\in K_{a}^{\rho}$  if and only if  $\eta^{z,L}$  merges into  $\eta^{0,L}$  before exiting  $B_{\rho}(0)$  and  $\eta^{z,R}$  hits  $\mathbbm{R}$  before leaving  $B_{\rho}(0)$ .
That is,  $K^{\rho}$  is defined in the same way as  $K_{a}^{\rho}$  but with  $h$  in place of  $h_{a}$ .
By definition,  $K^{\rho}$  is a.s. determined by  $h|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$ .
A basic Radon-Nikodym estimate for the GFF (see, e.g., the proof of [MS16a, Proposition 3.4] shows that the following is true for each  $\rho>0$ .
•
If  $a<-\rho$ , then the laws of  $h_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  and  $h|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  are mutually absolutely continuous.
•
The total variation distance between the laws of  $h_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  and  $h|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  tends to zero as  $a\rightarrow-\infty$ .
In particular,
$\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(K_{a}^{\rho},\preceq_{a}|_{K_{a}^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}}}}\right)\rightarrow\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(K^{\rho},\preceq|_{K^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}}}}\right)\quad\text{in total variation as $a\rightarrow-\infty$}.$
(A.49)
Lemma A.13.
Let  $r>0$  and let  $p\in(0,1)$ . There exists  $\rho=\rho(r,p)>r$  such that
$\mathbbm{P}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K^{\rho}}}\right]\geq p\quad\text{and}$
(A.50)
$\liminf_{a\rightarrow-\infty}\mathbbm{P}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K_{a}^{\rho}}}\right]\geq p.$
(A.51)
Proof.
Due to the total variation convergence  $K_{a}^{\rho}\rightarrow K^{\rho}$ , it suffices to show that there exists  $\rho=\rho(r,p)>r$  such that (A.50) holds.
To prove this, we will first show that  $K^{1}$  contains some neighborhood of 0 with probability at least  $p$  then use a scaling argument.
Choose  $a_{0}\in\mathbbm{N}$  with  $a_{0}<-1$ . Since the laws of  $h_{a_{0}}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  and  $h|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  are mutually absolutely continuous, also the laws of  $K_{a_{0}}^{1}$  and  $K^{1}$  are mutually absolutely continuous.
Since  $\eta_{a_{0}}$  is a chordal space-filling SLEκ, a.s.  $K_{a_{0}}^{1}$  contains some neighborhood of 0 in  $\mathbbm{H}$ .
Hence for any  $q\in(0,1)$  there exists  $\varepsilon>0$  such that  $\mathbbm{P}[B_{\varepsilon}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset\eta_{a_{0}}^{1}]\geq q$ .
By taking  $q$  to be sufficiently close to 1 (depending on  $p$ ) we infer that there exists  $\varepsilon>0$  such that
$\mathbbm{P}[B_{\varepsilon}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K^{1}]\geq p.$
(A.52)
Due to the scale invariance of the law of  $h$ , we have  $\rho K^{1}\overset{d}{=}K^{\rho}$  for each rational  $\rho>0$ .
Therefore (A.50) for  $\rho$  a rational number slightly larger than  $r/\varepsilon$  follows from (A.52).
∎
Proof of Proposition A.10.
Each  $\eta_{a}$  is a continuous curve which satisfies the conditions of the proposition statement with  $h_{a}$  in place of  $h$ .
Due to the total variation convergence (A.49), we infer that for each  $\rho>0$ , there is a unique curve  $\overline{\eta}^{\rho}$  mapping some time interval  $[T^{\rho},S^{\rho}]$  into  $K^{\rho}$  which satisfies  $\eta(0)=0$  and  $\operatorname{area}\eta([s,t])=t-s$  for each  $s<t$  and such that  $\overline{\eta}^{\rho}$  hits the points of  $K^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$  in the order specified by  $\preceq$ .
By (A.50) of Lemma A.13 and since  $r$  can be made arbitrarily large, it follows that the sets  $K^{\rho}$  a.s. increase to all of  $\mathbbm{C}$  as  $\rho\rightarrow\infty$ . In particular, a.s.  $S^{\rho}\rightarrow-\infty$  and  $T^{\rho}\rightarrow\infty$  as  $\rho\rightarrow\infty$ .
We therefore get a random continuous curve  $\eta$  from  $-\infty$  to  $\infty$  which satisfies the conditions in the first assertion of the lemma.
Furthermore, by the scale and translation invariance of the law of  $h$  we get that the law of the ordering  $\preceq$  is invariant under scaling by rational scaling factors and translation by rational elements of  $\mathbbm{R}$  (we need to restrict to rationals at this point since we defined our ordering using  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$ ).
This shows that the law of  $\eta$ , viewed modulo time parametrization, is invariant under rational scalings and translations.
By (A.51) of Lemma A.13 and (A.49), we get that  $\preceq_{a}|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  converges to  $\preceq|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  in the total variation sense as  $a\rightarrow-\infty$ .
It remains to show that the law of  $\eta$ , viewed modulo time parametrization, is in fact invariant under all scalings and translations, not just rational ones. To prove this, we observe that if  $C>0$ , then the argument above works equally well with  $C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$  in place of  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$ . Let  $\eta^{C}$  be the curve obtained in the same way as  $\eta$  but with  $C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$  in place of  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$ .
Then the law of  $\eta^{C}$ , viewed modulo time parametrization, is invariant under scalings and translations by rational multiples of  $C$ .
On the other hand, replacing  $\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$  by  $C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}$  does not change the curves  $\eta_{a}$ . From the total variation convergence  $\preceq_{a}^{C}|_{C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}\rightarrow\preceq^{C}|_{C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}$  (in obvious notation) for each  $r>0$  we therefore get that  $\eta^{C}\overset{d}{=}\eta$ . Since  $C$  is arbitrary we now conclude the proof.
∎

Instructions for reporting errors
We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
methods listed below:
Click the "Report Issue" (
) button, located in the page header.
Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
all.
Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
We gratefully acknowledge support from
our major funders,
member institutions, ,
and all contributors.
